grh_1e7249a81a035c7d4e5d.title: Anne Bonny's Gold
paragraphs: Newlyweds Ralph and Queenie Quince sail to a Caribbean island with what Ralph believes is an authentic Anne Bonny treasure map. After rescuing worldly adventurer Harry Bennett from the sea, they enlist his help, unaware that Skipper Sampson and his men are watching the hunt and intend to steal the treasure once it is found. Harry discovers the plot, sabotages and sinks the gang's launch, and leaves the would-be thieves stranded while Ralph keeps working through the map's clues. Their digging appears to fail until Harry notices that the map is dated July 22, 1718: the clue depends on the sun striking a specific spot on that same date each year, so their February search was hundreds of feet off. The three plan to return on July 22, confident they finally know where Anne Bonny's gold is buried, while Harry asks only for the chance to pocket a few doubloons when it is uncovered.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on May 4, 1979. It is listed as episode 65 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Fletcher Markle, Hans Conried, Joan McCall, [[person|john-dehner|John Dehner]], and Lou Horne. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Alan Caillou as writer, and Richard Widmark as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_1ed3d0de7e0451f068e7.title: Carmilla
paragraphs: In Vienna after the First World War, Amy befriends the beautiful and mysterious Carmilla, whose face matches the woman from a terrifying vision Amy experienced as a child. Carmilla becomes intensely attached to her while Amy grows weak, suffers strange nighttime sensations and develops a small mark on her throat. An old family portrait reveals Carmilla's exact likeness to Countess Karnstein, and a visiting general describes how a similar young woman preyed upon his own daughter. A doctor orders that Amy never be left alone, and the adults trace the mystery to the Karnstein tomb. There they identify Carmilla and the long-dead countess as the same vampire and destroy her while Amy lies barely alive. Amy recovers, but years later the memory of Carmilla still frightens and haunts her.

grh_1e79c41ae04e7b653e73.title: Always Yours
paragraphs: After two years apart during the war, Gail Sloan breaks her engagement to serviceman Larry Warnock and becomes involved with older hospital doctor Graham, believing the distance has changed her feelings. Larry unexpectedly returns home suffering another attack of malaria and admits to Dr. Christian that losing Gail has left him with nothing to come home to. Meanwhile Graham pressures Gail into an immediate elopement across the state line. On the trip she realizes she has made a mistake, slips away from him at a bus stop and walks through the snow back to Rivers End. At Dr. Christian's office she and Larry finally speak honestly: he still wants a future with her, and she still loves him. Their reconciliation ends with Gail repeating the sign-off from Larry's wartime letters, 'always yours.'
